s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with chronic lower abdominal pain
salient_findings: Hard, adherent, and painless mass on vaginal palpation
Nodular solid mass with enhancing vessels on CT
key_facts: 37-year-old woman
Lower abdominal pain for 4 months
Hard, adherent, and painless mass on vaginal palpation
Normal complete blood count
Normal serum electrolytes
Normal creatinine and urea
6.0 × 7.6 × 6.0 cm solid mass on transvaginal ultrasonography
7.4 cm nodular solid mass on CT
Attenuation values rising from 20 HU to 70 HU on delayed images
Multiple tortuous enhancing vessels at the periphery
Mass indents posterior uterine wall without invasion of adjacent organs
No lymphadenopathy

salient_findings: Hard, adherent, and painless mass on vaginal palpation
Nodular solid mass with enhancing vessels on CT

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subserosal uterine fibroid suspected based on location and imaging features

shortlist.label: Ovarian fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with chronic lower abdominal pain and solid mass on imaging

shortlist.label: Uterine adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Solid mass located between the uterus and the rectum with multiple tortuous enhancing vessels

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large solid mass with attenuation values rising from 20 HU to 70 HU on delayed images

shortlist.label: Ovarian granulosa cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with chronic lower abdominal pain and normal laboratory tests

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a hard, adherent, and painless mass on vaginal palpation, along with imaging features showing a solid mass located between the uterus and the rectum that indents the posterior uterine wall without invasion of adjacent organs, is consistent with a uterine leiomyoma (fibroid). The attenuation values and presence of tortuous enhancing vessels also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ovarian fibroma
rejected.why: Ovarian fibroma is less likely given the mass's location and its effect on the uterine wall.

rejected.label: Uterine adenomatoid tumor
rejected.why: Uterine adenomatoid tumors are typically smaller and less likely to cause significant uterine indentation.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: Aggressive angiomyxoma is a rare tumor that usually presents with more aggressive features and invasion of surrounding tissues, not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Ovarian granulosa cell tumor
rejected.why: Ovarian granulosa cell tumor would more likely present with hormonal imbalance symptoms and different imaging characteristics.
